thread:
maria_support: Customer (AcmeAnalytics) reporting intermittent 502/504s and a few 503 spikes from hosted inference since ~09:10 UTC. They're seeing it from multiple regions. sample log attached from their SDK: 

maria_support: <log>
{"error":"502 Bad Gateway","request_id":"r-abc123","latency_ms":1204}
{"error":"504 Gateway Timeout","request_id":"r-def456","latency_ms":30000}
</log>

maria_support: Repro steps they shared: batch embeddings (~250 items), concurrency=60, client retries enabled with exponential backoff. They also said failures seem to correlate with periods of higher traffic.

jordan_oncall: Thanks — I'm looking at our edge LB metrics now. Seeing a short spike in upstream 5xx around 09:08-09:12 UTC, higher connection resets on proxy -> gateway tier. No full host OOMs. Can you share SDK request/headers sample?

maria_support: Pasted an abbreviated curl they used: 

curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer xxx" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -d '{"model":"embed-lite-v1","input":["...repeat 250 items..."]}'

maria_support: They have client-side concurrency=60 and no client-side batching per-request (they send batches of 250).

nate_infra: That pattern can cause head-of-line contention in our embedding pool when large batches land simultaneously. Two quick asks: 1) what's the rate per-second for those bursts? 2) can we get proxy logs for those request_ids? I'll tail the LB logs for that window.

maria_support: Customer says ~180 rps at peak during the spike window. I attached their request_ids: r-abc123, r-def456, r-ghi789.

deploy-bot: Deployment 2026-03-17T08:50 UTC: rolling update of edge-proxy 1.12.3 -> 1.12.4 completed at 08:55 UTC in us-west-2. No failed pods.

jordan_oncall: Noting rollout just before the window — could be related but infra metrics didn't flag increased errors cluster-wide. Nate — here's proxy log snippet for r-def456: 

<log>
[09:11:24.512] client_conn_closed peer=10.0.4.192 id=r-def456 status=RST_STREAM code=11 upstream=pool-embed-17 err=write ECONNRESET
[09:11:24.513] upstream_retry count=1 target=embed-worker-17
[09:11:54.799] request_timed_out id=r-def456 duration=30000ms route=/v1/embeddings
</log>

nate_infra: Looks like a connection reset from embed-worker-17 followed by a timeout. Checking worker logs now — seeing a momentary spike in per-GPU queue length and a few long GC pauses in the embedding runner process. Possible CPU stall on host.

sophie_cs: I just spoke to Acme — they're asking for a mitigation while we investigate. They want to avoid client retries exacerbating the issue. Any short-term recommended config?

jordan_oncall: Two short-term mitigations: 1) recommend client reduce concurrency to ~12-20 and split their 250-item batches into smaller chunks (e.g., 16-32) to reduce per-request processing time. 2) add jittered backoff and cap retries to 2. I'll draft suggested language.

maria_support: Suggested message for customer: 

"We're seeing upstream worker resets during your peak. As a temporary mitigation please reduce concurrent connections and split large batches into smaller requests (16-32 items). Also enable jittered backoff and limit retries to 2. We're investigating the embedding workers and will update you in 2 hours."

sophie_cs: OK sending that now. Will follow up if they push back on latency impact.

nate_infra: On infra side: opening a short-term mitigation ticket to drain embed-worker-17, reprovision a fresh instance (suspect CPU stall). Also increasing embedding-pool autoscale threshold to allow faster spin-up during bursts.

jordan_oncall: I'll also add a temporary rate-limit rule on the downstream proxy for very large batch payloads (> 1MB payload OR items >200) to fail fast with 413 so retries don't cascade. We should coordinate with Product before rolling to prod.

maria_support: Noted. I've updated the customer with the mitigation steps and asked for confirmation after they change settings.

sophie_cs: Customer responded: "we'll drop concurrency to 15 and chunk to 25 per request; testing now." :thumbsup:

nate_infra: After draining and reprovisioning the worker, initial metrics look back to baseline. No further 5xx in the last 8 minutes.

jordan_oncall: Great. Action items: 
- nate_infra: follow up with host-level postmortem on CPU stall / GC (ETA 24h)
- eng_platform: review edge-proxy rollout timing vs LB steady-state (assigning next)
- product/security: review temporary payload rate-limit change (notify before prod)
- maria_support/sophie_cs: keep customer updated, confirm full recovery end-to-end

maria_support: I'll close the support ticket after a 1 hour clean window and confirm. Thank you all. :raised_hands:
